plan.contextChunk: This figure places three small sketched graphs side by side, labeled (a), (b), and (c), each showing curves that rise from left to right on an unmarked vertical axis above a horizontal axis whose tip is labeled n; no numeric ticks appear anywhere. Panel (a) carries three curves: the highest is labeled c2 g(n), the lowest c1 g(n), and a third labeled f(n) weaves between them, dipping and crossing near the left edge before settling into the corridor between the other two. A dashed vertical segment drops from that crossing region to a tick on the n axis marked n0, and the expression f(n) = Theta(g(n)) is printed below the plot. Panel (b) has two curves, the upper labeled c g(n) and the lower labeled f(n); f(n) oscillates sharply at small n, meets c g(n) at the dashed line standing over the tick n0, and runs beneath it from there on, with f(n) = O(g(n)) underneath. Panel (c) reverses the roles, putting f(n) above and c g(n) below after they touch at the dashed n0 line, and is captioned f(n) = Omega(g(n)). Read against one another, the three panels turn on where the labeled curve sits relative to the scaled comparison function once n passes n0, giving the geometric intuition behind bounding a function from both sides, from above only, and from below only.

interactionPlan.concept: An asymptotic bound (Theta, O, or Omega) only requires f(n) to stay within, below, or above a constant-scaled copy of g(n) once n passes some threshold n0 — constant factors and small-input wiggles are irrelevant.
elements: horizontal axis labeled n with an arrowhead, no numeric ticks
vertical axis (unlabeled, no ticks)
wiggly curve f(n): oscillates sharply at small n, then rises steadily to the right, labeled f(n)
smooth monotonically increasing reference curve g(n) (used to build the scaled comparison curves)
Theta view: lower envelope curve c1·g(n) and upper envelope curve c2·g(n) forming a corridor around f(n), both labeled
O view: single upper curve c·g(n) above f(n) after n0, labeled
Omega view: single lower curve c·g(n) below f(n) after n0, labeled
dashed vertical line at the threshold n0 dropping to a tick labeled n0 on the n-axis
shaded permitted region for f(n): the corridor between c1·g and c2·g (Theta), the area below c·g (O), or the area above c·g (Omega)
red violation markers on f(n) wherever it leaves the permitted region for n >= n0
caption under the plot: f(n) = Theta(g(n)), f(n) = O(g(n)), or f(n) = Omega(g(n)) matching the active view

interactions.label: Bound type
interactions.teaches: Theta traps f(n) in a two-sided corridor between c1·g and c2·g; O only demands an upper ceiling c·g; Omega only demands a lower floor c·g — the same f and g can satisfy different bound types depending on which side(s) are constrained

interactions.label: Threshold n0
interactions.teaches: The bound only has to hold for n >= n0; dragging n0 right shows that the wild oscillations and crossings at small n are simply ignored, while dragging it too far left exposes violations to its right that must be eliminated by choosing n0 large enough

interactions.label: Constant multiplier on g(n)
interactions.teaches: We are free to scale g(n) by any positive constant: in Theta the slider widens/narrows the c1·g..c2·g corridor proportionally, in O it raises/lowers the ceiling, in Omega it raises/lowers the floor — a bound exists as long as some constant makes the permitted region eventually contain f(n)

demo_steps.title: Two-sided bound (Theta)
demo_steps.narration: In the Theta view, f(n) is squeezed into the shaded corridor between c1·g(n) and c2·g(n) for all n to the right of the dashed n0 line; the wiggles and crossings before n0 do not matter.

demo_steps.title: n0 only has to be large enough
demo_steps.narration: Drag n0 leftward: red violation markers appear where f(n) escapes the corridor to the right of the line, because the small-n oscillation is no longer being ignored. Slide n0 back right until no violations remain — that is all the definition demands.

demo_steps.title: Upper bound only (O)
demo_steps.narration: Switch to O: now only a ceiling c·g(n) is required, so the shaded permitted region is everything below it. Dragging the constant slider up or down moves the ceiling and shows how a single constant creates the upper bound.

demo_steps.title: Lower bound only (Omega)
demo_steps.narration: Switch to Omega: the roles flip and the permitted region is everything above the floor c·g(n). The same f and g that gave an upper bound now give a lower bound, illustrating that O and Omega constrain opposite sides.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Asymptotic notation discards constant factors and small-input behavior: a bound holds if some constant-scaled g(n) eventually (for all n >= n0) traps, caps, or floors f(n), regardless of how f misbehaves before that threshold.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Render one plot at a time that morphs with the boundType toggle rather than three static side-by-side panels. Horizontal n-axis with arrowhead and a single dashed-line tick n0; vertical axis plain. f(n) is a hand-drawn wiggly curve: a couple of sharp oscillations near the left edge, then a smooth steady rise. g(n) is a clean monotone increasing curve (gentle super-linear rise). In Theta mode draw two smooth curves c1·g (below f) and c2·g (above f) and shade the corridor between them in a soft blue; in O mode draw c·g above f and shade the region below it in soft green; in Omega mode draw c·g below f and shade the region above it in soft amber. The dashed n0 line is gray and vertical; the n0 tick label sits under the axis. Mark any point where f(n) leaves the shaded permitted region at n >= n0 with a small red dot so violations are unmistakable. Curve labels (f(n), c·g(n), c1·g(n), c2·g(n)) in italic serif math style near the right end of each curve; the matching equation caption (f(n) = Theta(g(n)) etc.) centered under the plot. Keep axes free of numeric ticks to match the textbook sketch.
